overall_verdict: FAIL: three blocking defects, namely a false claim about the design sources (no source states 44 rows), a PARTIAL example that cannot happen under the 5-call cap pinned by T4, and an uncited rule that the plain-text export writes UNKNOWN where the screen writes unknown. The required coverage items are all present and the owner decisions are respected.

findings.finding: False claim presented as fact: 'no design source states 44'. The design package PLAN.md:57 says 'Wide target around 44-52 rows; compact target around 36-44'. The cited DESIGN-CONTRACT.md:8 and concepts.md:36 do give the 48/42 export heights, but the claim that no design source mentions 44 is wrong, and UX-OQ-2 (EXPERIENCE.md:523) is built on it.
findings.fix: Replace it with: 'The exports are 48 rows (160) and 42 rows (116/80) (DESIGN-CONTRACT.md:8, concepts.md:36). PLAN.md:57 gives targets of 44-52 rows (wide) and 36-44 (compact), and no source defines the 44-row contract's contents (OQ-14).' Update UX-OQ-2 to match.

findings.finding: Wrong behaviour versus the acceptance tests. The UJ-1 failure path says that if page.hasMore is still true at the call cap, 'PARTIAL: collected 100 of reported 412' appears. The cap is 5 subprocesses per cycle at 100 rows per page (adapter-contract.md:3, :25), so the cap is reached at 500 collected rows, and T4 pins 'PARTIAL: collected 500 of reported T' (acceptance-tests.md:12; prd.md:175). Under the cap, 412 reported rows are read in full within 5 pages, so the example cannot occur, and an implementer could copy it into a fixture.
findings.fix: Use 'PARTIAL: collected 500 of reported 1240 (newest first; oldest rows not read; long-running active workers may be among them)', or any reported T above 500.

findings.finding: Uncited rule that contradicts the document's own export rule. UJ-4 says the plain-text export writes missing values as the string 'UNKNOWN'. The UNKNOWN-string rule belongs to the JSON snapshot (snapshot-export-schema.md:10; prd.md:237). The text export is 'exactly the view on screen' (prd.md:46, prd.md:68), the screen shows the literal 'unknown' (rendering-rules.md:51), and EXPERIENCE.md:267 itself says the export has the same content as the screen. No source gives the text export an uppercase sentinel.
findings.location: EXPERIENCE.md:469 (vs EXPERIENCE.md:267; sources: snapshot-export-schema.md:10, prd.md:46, rendering-rules.md:51)
findings.fix: Say that the text export writes missing values exactly as the screen does ('unknown', or 'unknown (absent in source)' for inspector fields), and keep 'UNKNOWN' only for the JSON snapshot.

findings.finding: A source contradiction is resolved without being flagged. rendering-rules.md:17 says the fixture header reads 'SYNTHETIC FIXTURE <variant>, not Orca data', while T50 and the PRD (acceptance-tests.md:44; prd.md:85, :126) say 'synthetic fixture, not live evidence'. The UX builds a hybrid, 'synthetic fixture, not live evidence (<variant>)', and calls it 'the T50 label, verbatim', without recording that the spec's own header string differs. It satisfies T50, but it silently overrides the spec header string.
findings.fix: Add a UX-OQ (or cite it as a CONTRADICTION) naming both strings, and keep the T50 substring as the minimum.

findings.finding: The PROPOSED default for worktree naming fails T20 as written. T20 and FR-4 need a rendered screen in which two rows sharing a worktreeId each name it, and a row with no worktree shows 'worktree unknown' (acceptance-tests.md:17; prd.md:148). The UX puts the worktree only in the inspector and the export, yet EXPERIENCE.md:241 still says 'A missing worktree reads worktree unknown' in the ledger section, with no ledger cell to hold it. It is correctly raised as UX-OQ-8, so it is not blocking.
findings.fix: State in UX-OQ-8 that the PROPOSED inspector-only option does not satisfy T20 as worded, and move the 'worktree unknown' sentence to the inspector and export rules.

findings.finding: The PROPOSED --ascii replacement of every non-ASCII source character with '?' breaks 'full IDs in the selected detail' and the copy-the-ID climax (UJ-3) for any CJK or emoji ID, and it is not limited to the screen. That is a loss in the inspector and possibly the export, which T24/T27 require to be full.
findings.fix: Limit the '?' replacement to cut list cells on screen, and show non-ASCII characters in the inspector and export as an unambiguous escape (for example U+XXXX), or leave the export unaffected by --ascii.

findings.finding: The 80-115 column restatement of B omits the spec's invariant lines 'Questions stay until explicit resolution.' and 'No reply observed is not delivery failure.', which rendering-rules.md:42 says stay. The B shrink order (EXPERIENCE.md:165-168) also does not protect them.
findings.fix: Add the two invariant lines to the 80-115 row, and list them among B's never-dropped lines.

findings.finding: The state vocabulary's 'exact rendering' for failed lists only 'FAILED (<exit code or timeout>)'. T32 pins 'FAILED (shape)' (acceptance-tests.md:21), and adapter-contract.md:50 counts invalid JSON as a failure. The row-level states 'order unknown' and 'conflict (time went back)' (T22) and the inspector's 'n unrecognised keys' (adapter-contract.md:38) are also missing.
findings.fix: Add FAILED (shape), the T22 row flags and the unrecognised-keys line to the vocabulary and the inspector field list.

findings.finding: The PROPOSED loading state shows 'collected 0 / reported unknown' before any poll. It is honest because of the unknown denominator, but it is the one place a not-observed state renders as 0, against the stance at EXPERIENCE.md:33.
findings.fix: Use 'collected none yet / reported unknown (not yet polled)', or keep it and say explicitly why it does not breach NFR-11.

findings.finding: The full PARTIAL sentence is said never to be cut (EXPERIENCE.md:441), but it sits on a one-row status line that folds into the footer when height falls (EXPERIENCE.md:161). At 80 columns the sentence (about 110 cells) cannot fit on one row. Only the PARTIAL token is spec-protected (rendering-rules.md:19).
findings.fix: Say that the PARTIAL token in COUNTS is never cut and that the full sentence wraps, or is complete in the inspector or export.

findings.finding: The footer anatomy has 'a light rule, then the key list' (two rows), but the 44-row budget gives the footer one row (row 44), after the ledger frame bottom at row 43.
findings.fix: State that the ledger frame bottom doubles as the footer rule, or add a row to the budget.

findings.finding: The freshness-strip colours do not cover the 'NOT AVAILABLE (orca binary not found)' state, which EXPERIENCE.md:184 and :291 use.
findings.fix: Give NOT AVAILABLE a token (warn or bad), alongside its word.

findings.finding: There is no help key, yet the voice table and the spec need help text ('a completed Task can still own a live terminal', rendering-rules.md:52; the per-process caps note in help, adapter-contract.md:62). The UX never says where help text is shown.
findings.fix: Name the surface that carries help text (for example the inspector or the --help output), or record it as an open question.

findings.finding: The keyboard table is headed 'spec, rendering-rules.md:20', but it includes entries the spec does not list (Ctrl-C, Backspace, and the inspector's m/e/q behaviour) without a PROPOSED label.
Citation drift: FR-16 is cited as prd.md:86, which is the glossary row; FR-16 is at prd.md:235. The statement that '--once ... writes one snapshot' is an inference with no source.
findings.fix: Cite prd.md:235, and mark the --once snapshot behaviour PROPOSED.
